title: Icons in icons only task manager reduce to unusable size when Panel is filled up with other widgets
line: On a crowded panel, Task Manager icons keep their full size and the tasks scroll, with the active or alerting task always brought into view, instead of shrinking to tiny slivers.
explanation: Tasks had no minimum size, so when the panel gave the Task Manager only its minimum length (one task) every task was squeezed to fit, leaving icons a few pixels wide on horizontal and vertical panels alike. Each task now keeps at least its icon size (minimum width on horizontal panels, minimum height on vertical ones); when they don't fit, the task list is clipped inside the Task Manager and scrolls, so the panel layout itself is unchanged (unlike the reverted scrollable-panel change). The active task, a task demanding attention and an app being launched are scrolled into view, the clipped edges fade out to show there is more, and the wheel only scrolls the tasks when it has no other configured action (otherwise Shift+wheel or horizontal scrolling does).

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: scroll tasks instead of shrinking them to nothing

When the panel was crowded, tasks shrank with no lower limit and their
icons became unusable. Tasks now keep their icon size and scroll, with
faded edges, keeping the active or attention-seeking task in view.

BUG: 447603

media.caption: Master: panel crowded with Global Menu and 9 clocks, the six windows' tasks are squeezed into thin slivers.
With the fix: same panel, one task at full icon size, its edges faded where the other tasks are scrolled out of view.
Master, same panel moved to the left edge: the tasks are squeezed into thin horizontal lines.
With the fix, vertical panel: the active task keeps a usable size and the others scroll.

With the fix: activating System Monitor, Info Center and Menu Editor brings each task into view; the wheel scrolls through the tasks with faded edges; Konsole demanding attention scrolls into view in orange.

review.text: Making the Task Manager scroll internally once tasks reach minimum icon size is the right VDG-approved approach and avoids the regressions of panel-wide scrolling, with solid handling of active/attention auto-scrolling, vertical panels, and mirrored layouts. However, there are a few concrete QML bugs in main.qml and an accessibility gap in Task.qml that should be fixed before merging.
changes: In applets/taskmanager/qml/main.qml, filter out non-positive Layout.minimumWidth/Layout.minimumHeight entries (such as taskRepeater, whose default Layout.minimumWidth/Height is -1) when computing contentMinimumWidth and contentMinimumHeight, and guard widthOccupation/heightOccupation > 0 so empty lists do not yield -Infinity and single-stripe lists are not off by 1 px.

In applets/taskmanager/qml/main.qml, bind fadeMask's layer.enabled to tmf.layer.enabled so an offscreen layer is not allocated when there is no overflow, and guard fadeLength against zero width/height so GradientStop.position never receives NaN.

In applets/taskmanager/qml/Task.qml, call tasksRoot.showTask(task) when a non-popup task receives keyboard focus (e.g., activeFocus && !containsMouse) so Tab/keyboard navigation brings clipped tasks into view.
